title: sms_send_outcomes answer
description: The structuredContent of the phone's sms_send_outcomes tool (ADR-CVM-010). How each held text ended, one item per recipient, oldest first, after the cursor that was passed. An item never holds a number, a name or a text: it names its recipient by position in the read-back. Nothing is deleted on the phone until a later call passes back this answer's cursor, so an answer lost on the way is given again, with the same ids. After sent, a later item for the same recipient can say delivered or failed; the latest item for a recipient is its outcome.

outcomes.description: Oldest first. Empty when nothing has ended since the cursor: the caller marks sms_send_outcomes as a poll, so an empty answer is counted, not logged.

cursor.description: Opaque, as in sms_since: passed in the next call exactly as it came, never read, compared or built. That call acknowledges every outcome here and this answer's dropped count. An answer carrying an outcome or a dropped count gives a cursor never given before.

more.description: true when more outcomes are waiting than one answer holds. Call again at once, with this cursor.

dropped.description: Outcomes the phone dropped before they were acknowledged: over 500 kept, or older than 7 days; a marker or outcome file that could not be read counts at least one, and the voice then says a text may have been sent. The count can be a little high, never low, and is cleared only when a call passes the cursor of an answer that carried it. 0 when none.

reset.description: true when the cursor passed was not one this phone gave, as after a reinstall. The answer then starts at the oldest outcome kept, so some may come a second time with the same id: the caller drops any id it has already seen.

id.description: <install>-<number>, as sms_since's ids, from a sequence of its own. The same outcome keeps its id each time it is given again. Compared whole, never parsed.

token.description: The token sms_send_request answered with, so the caller ties the outcome to the request it made. Opaque, and already spent: it can never confirm again.

recipient.description: The recipient's position in the read-back, after duplicates were dropped; 1 for a text to one recipient. Never a number or a name: right after the undo the voice still has the read-back and names them; a later poll says 'recipient 2'.

outcome.description: sent: Android reported every part sent. delivered: every part also has a delivery report saying so; some networks send none, so a text may stay sent. stopped: cancelled, held when the app stopped, or not sent because the phone could not save the send; never handed to Android. failed: Android reported a part failed, or refused the text at once. unknown: the app stopped after handing it to Android and cannot tell; it is never sent again. After sent, a later item may say delivered or failed: the latest item is the outcome.

at.description: When the phone learned the outcome, ISO 8601 with the phone's offset.

enum: the app restarted while it was held
the phone could not save the send, so it did not send it
it may have been sent; check the text app
reason.description: A fixed phrase for the voice, never free text, so no number, name, text or raw Android error can pass. ADR-CVM-010 lists which phrases belong to which outcome.
